beats.narration_text: Hello. This is Liam, in for Bear. You can paste the Prompt Engineering prompt into a Claude Project and ask for practice questions. The prompt includes starter knowledge. No extra upload is needed to begin. Let us walk through the source, not a recorded live session.

props.text: How do I predict the real exam?

beats.narration_text: Create a Claude Project for Prompt Engineering practice. Open its instructions, and paste everything below Project instructions begin from the current prompt. Save the instructions, then start a new conversation in that project. This film illustrates the written workflow; it does not show a tested live Claude session.

lines: Create a Claude Project for Prompt Engineering for
Generative AI practice. Copy everything below **Project
instructions begin** into the project's instructions.

beats.source_excerpt: Create a Claude Project for Prompt Engineering for Generative AI practice. Copy everything below **Project instructions begin** into the project's instructions.

beats.narration_text: Begin small. Ask for one case with five specific questions, and ask the coach to wait for your answers. The instructions default to one case. You can also request one multiple-answer question, a topic drill, or a full practice paper.

props.title: Source excerpt · Choose one practice mode
lines: Honor the learner's requested mode: one case, one multiple-
answer question, a topic drill, or a full practice exam.
Default to one case if no quantity is specified.

qc.sparse_reason: Read-only source excerpt; intentional few lines, not a live app simulation.

beats.source_excerpt: Honor the learner's requested mode: one case, one multiple-answer question, a topic drill, or a full practice exam. Default to one case if no quantity is specified.

beats.narration_text: The full paper has one hundred points. Five case questions contribute fifty. Ten multiple-answer questions contribute fifty more. Each case must print five specific questions. Short numbered answers are enough; this is not an open essay.

props.title: Source excerpt · 100 points, split equally
lines: Part A: five case-style questions, 10 points each, 50 points
total.
Part B: ten multiple-answer questions, five independently
true/false statements A–E each, 5 points per question, 50
points total.

qc.sparse_reason: Read-only source excerpt; intentional few lines, not a live app simulation.

beats.source_excerpt:
Part A: five case-style questions, 10 points each, 50 points total.
Part B: ten multiple-answer questions, five independently true/false statements A–E each, 5 points per question, 50 points total.

beats.narration_text: Check the case before answering. Its five questions should ask you to identify a supported defect, name the concept, propose a check, rewrite the instruction, and explain the consequence plainly. The points are three, two, two, two, and one.

props.title: Source excerpt · Five specific questions per case
lines: Ask exactly five specific, numbered questions about the
supplied case. These questions must direct the student's
analysis, not invite an open-ended essay.

qc.sparse_reason: Read-only source excerpt; intentional few lines, not a live app simulation.

beats.source_excerpt: Ask exactly five specific, numbered questions about the supplied case. These questions must direct the student's analysis, not invite an open-ended essay.

beats.narration_text: For multiple-answer practice, judge each of the five statements independently. Any number can be true. A true statement checked correctly earns one point, and a false statement left unchecked correctly also earns one. Do not hunt for an answer pattern.

props.title: Source excerpt · Five independent statements
lines: For each multiple-answer item give a short setup and five
independently judgeable statements. Any number from zero
through five may be true.

qc.sparse_reason: Read-only source excerpt; intentional few lines, not a live app simulation.

beats.source_excerpt: For each multiple-answer item give a short setup and five independently judgeable statements. Any number from zero through five may be true.

beats.narration_text: Submit your attempt before requesting feedback. The coach should not reveal the diagnosis or worked solution beside the question. After your attempt, it can give targeted practice feedback and rubric scores. Private instructor keys never belong in the student-facing project.

practice feedback; do not reveal unrelated or instructor-
only keys.

beats.narration_text: The embedded starter notes make this prompt self-contained. They cover prompt contracts, tool permissions, agent loops, and other taught mechanisms. No extra upload or live API call is needed. Optional course files can improve source-specific fidelity, but the coach must not pretend to read files you did not supply.

props.title: Source excerpt · Self-contained starter knowledge
lines: Prioritize prompting, agents, loops, generation, tools and
integration. Evaluation supports those mechanisms; do not
turn this into the Computational Skepticism course.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste the instructions into your project and ask for one case with five specific questions, without answers. Check the five questions and ten-point rubric. Then submit your attempt and inspect the feedback. Treat this as practice, not a prediction of the real exam.
